authoring_rules: Sixth held-out set, for the summarizer-candidate decision of CANDIDATE_V5.md (arms BASE, V2, V4 diagnostic, V5).
Written from the source at the pinned commits before any engine, search, ranking or summarizer ran on these repositories. Only a name-only index (candidate pool names, check.py) was built.
Same rules as sets 1-5: developer phrasing; gold = the function(s) that directly answer; decoys = plausible wrong functions (same stems, the caller or the helper, a sibling).
No question contains its gold symbol's name or every word of it (check.py).
Gold and decoys are library code, never test files; no property setter (#2) is gold or decoy.

Selection: 4 repositories none of sets 1-5 used, Python and TypeScript, each with >= 300 library functions (check.py). koajs/koa (103) and sindresorhus/ky (105) failed it and were replaced by elysiajs/elysia and oclif/core (approved).

questions.question: When the client follows a 3xx to another host, which fields are stripped from the next outgoing request, and why does a plain http-to-https upgrade keep the credentials?
After a 302 or 303 response, when does the follow-up request switch from POST to GET, and why is HEAD left alone?
How is the Location value of a 3xx turned into the next address to visit, including relative paths and a missing host or fragment?
How are HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY variables turned into mount patterns, and what does a wildcard in the bypass list do?
How does the library find out how many bytes an uploaded file object holds without reading it, falling back to seeking to the end?
When several mount patterns could match an address, how are they ordered so that ones with a port and longer hostnames win?
Where are credential-bearing fields like Authorization masked as [secure] when a request or its header collection is printed?
Which character set is used to decode raw header bytes, trying ascii, then utf-8, and finally latin-1?
Which quality-of-protection option is chosen from a digest challenge, and when does auth-int raise a not-implemented error?
How are dot and dot-dot segments removed from the route component of an address, following RFC 3986?
When streaming a body line by line, how are partial lines buffered across chunks and a trailing carriage return carried into the next piece?
How does a response pick how to decompress its body from the Content-Encoding values, chaining several when gzip and br are both listed?
How does a response throw an error on 4xx and 5xx codes, with a message naming the error class and the Location when it is a 3xx?
How does the library decide whether an outgoing body becomes raw bytes, a multipart form, a url-encoded form or JSON, and warn when bytes are passed as form data?
How are low-level connection-pool errors translated into the library's own exception types, picking the most specific match?
How is an integer total split into parts proportional to integer weights, honouring per-slot minimums so the parts add up exactly?
How does the terminal printer decide between truecolor, 256 and 16 colours from COLORTERM and TERM, and when does it turn colour off entirely?
How is a 24-bit RGB value reduced to the nearest index of the 256-colour cube, treating low-saturation values as grey?
How is the closest entry in a fixed colour table found for an RGB triple using a weighted redmean distance?
Given a byte count, how is the right power of 1000 or 1024 and its label like kB or MiB chosen?
How is user text made safe to embed among square-bracket style tags so it is not treated as formatting, including trailing backslashes?
How is the number of spaces per indent level of a code snippet worked out from the greatest common divisor of the even leading-space widths?
How are adjacent rendered pieces that share the same style merged into one to reduce the output written to the terminal?
How is a string broken into lines that each fit a given terminal column width when it contains double-width characters?
How is styled text shortened to a maximum width, adding an ellipsis character or padding with spaces when asked?
How is the rate of a running task in steps per second estimated from its recent samples?
How is the estimated time left for a task shown as h:mm:ss or a compact mm:ss, with dashes when it is unknown?
When printing an exception's stack frames, how is the highlighting language for each source file chosen, including files with no extension that start with a python shebang?
When a grid's columns are too wide for the screen, how are the widest wrappable columns shrunk step by step until everything fits?
How is a log record's severity name padded and styled before it is shown in the left column of the logging handler's output?
How is one stored cookie value looked up by name, optionally narrowed by domain and path, and what error is raised when two match?
How is the boundary token pulled out of a multipart/form-data Content-Type value that the caller supplied?
How is a relative address joined onto a client's base address so that a subpath in the base is preserved?
When parsing an address, why is :443 on https or :80 on http dropped, and what happens to a non-numeric port?
How is a pagination Link value with <uri>; rel=next entries split into a list of dicts?
How is a hostname validated and encoded, checking IPv4 and bracketed IPv6 literals and converting international names with IDNA?
When a response is iterated in fixed-size chunks, how are incoming byte pieces re-sliced and the remainder buffered?
How is the media type of an uploaded file guessed from its filename, defaulting to application/octet-stream?
How are booleans and None converted into form or query values, using JSON-style true/false and an empty string?
How is the total byte size of a multipart upload computed in advance, giving up when any file's size is unknown?
When calling a WSGI app in-process, how are empty byte strings at the start of its body iterator skipped?
How is the originating request attached to network errors raised inside a block of code?
How does a response choose the text decoding to use: an explicit setting, then the charset in Content-Type, then a default or an autodetect callable?
How does digest authentication react to a 401 challenge, building the credential header and replaying the request with any cookies set?
How are credentials for a host looked up in the user's .netrc file and sent as basic authorization when found?
How is a colour description like 'red', 'color(123)', '#ff0000' or 'rgb(1,2,3)' interpreted, rejecting numbers above 255?
How is a set of named styles loaded from an INI-style configuration file on disk?
Given a file path and optionally its contents, how is the highlighter language picked, falling back to the file extension?
How is one rendered line forced to an exact cell width, cropping the overflowing piece or padding with styled spaces?
How are tab characters in styled text replaced by the right number of spaces to reach the next tab stop, keeping styles?
How is one RGB value faded towards another by a cross-fade fraction?
How are :shortcode: names in text swapped for their emoji characters, with an optional text or emoji presentation variant?
How are wrapped lines aligned left, centre, right or fully justified to a width by distributing extra spaces between words?
How is a border style swapped for one that can actually be drawn on legacy Windows consoles or ASCII-only terminals?
Given text and an available width, where are the line breaks placed, folding words that are longer than a whole line?
How is a CSS-style spacing shorthand of one, two or four numbers expanded into top, right, bottom and left?
How does the pretty printer decide whether an object can be broken out over several lines, such as containers, dataclasses and attrs objects but not classes?
How is reading an already open binary file tracked as a task, recovering the total byte count from the task when it was not given?
What happens when output is piped to a program that exits early, so further writes fail with a closed pipe?
How are several text styles merged into one, with later ones taking precedence?

How is the incoming Cookie request header turned into a jar of values, decoding JSON-looking values and rejecting entries whose signature does not verify?
When a handler has set several cookies, how are they rendered into one or more Set-Cookie strings for the reply, skipping empty values?
How does the framework decide whether a text value is a safe integer, rejecting blanks and values longer than 16 digits?
How is the alternate form of a route with or without its trailing slash computed so both variants can be registered?
How is a route percent-encoded while keeping slashes, and colons and question marks for dynamic parameters?
How is a fast 32-bit hash of a string computed to identify plugins and hooks?
How are repeated lifecycle hooks with the same hash removed from a hook list when the same plugin is applied twice?
How are two nested configuration objects combined recursively, with options to skip keys, keep existing values or concatenate arrays, without touching frozen objects or class instances?
How is a nested object or array copied including symbol keys, guarding against circular references?

How is a plain object of fields and files converted into a multipart body, appending each array element separately and remembering the original values?

How is an incoming socket frame coerced from text into JSON, a number, a boolean or null before custom parse hooks run?

How are cached handler-inference results discarded after an idle delay, and why is this skipped on Cloudflare Workers?

How is a route with optional parameters like /a/:b?/:c? expanded into every concrete route the native router must register?

How is an uploaded part's MIME type compared against an allowed type pattern, including wildcards like image/*?
How is an uploaded blob accepted or rejected by minimum and maximum size and the allowed list of types?
How is the release track like beta or next worked out from a version string's prerelease tag, falling back to stable?
With flexible topic ordering, how is every reordering of a command's name parts generated so they can be typed in any order?
How is the CLI's binary name turned into an uppercase environment variable prefix, replacing @, slashes and dashes?
When a partial command id is typed in some order, how are candidate commands narrowed to those that accept every flag on the command line?
How is a lifecycle hook given a deadline, rejecting with a timed-out error if it takes too long?
When a command declares alternate names, how is each one registered, choosing between colliding commands by plugin priority and adding all its word orderings?
How is the usable width of the terminal determined, defaulting to 80 when not interactive and never going below 40?
When topics are separated by spaces, how are the leading words of argv joined into a command id, stopping at a flag or once a command expects positional arguments?
How is the process exit status attached to an error, defaulting to the configured or standard code 2?
How are the remedy hints shown after an error message laid out, as one line or an indented bullet list after 'Try this:'?
When two installed plugins provide a command with the same id, which one wins, with core plugins ordered by the package.json list and just-in-time plugins last?
How does the command-line parser read piped input without hanging when nothing is piped, using a short abort timer and caching the result globally?
How is a double-dash option on the command line resolved to its declared name, including aliases and the --no- negation of a boolean?
How is a single-letter option like -v matched to the option it abbreviates, honouring character aliases?
How is it enforced that two mutually incompatible options are not both given, ignoring options that only got their default value?
